task.title: Cancel finite recurrence intent through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/961 to expose exact-revision recurrence cancellation as a deterministic writable adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence identity and non-blank cancellation reason before storage access.
Delegate optimistic concurrency and lifecycle append to RecurrenceStore::cancel.
Emit cancellation-aware JSON and stable no-stdout failures without rejected appends.

attempts.diagnostic: Focused CLI tests failed because cancel was not a recognized recurrence subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added focused integration coverage for the issue contract before completing the production boundary.

attempts.summary: Implemented and refactored the bounded slice.
attempts.diagnostic: Implemented recurrence cancel parsing, validation, writable delegation, deterministic output, categorized diagnostics, tests, ADR-0083, and docs.
attempts.patch: Implemented the issue 961 contract in crates/vela-dev/src/lib.rs with focused tests and synchronized architecture and behavior documentation.

attempts.diagnostic: Independent read-only review and genuine exact-head CodeRabbit review reported no actionable comments; a rate-limit status was not accepted as sufficient evidence.
attempts.patch: Applied blocking findings where present, reran verification, required substantive review, and preserved zero unresolved review threads before merge.

outcome.summary: Issue 961 delivered the documented recurrence boundary with strict evidence, bounded authority, and verified merge provenance.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate for pull request 962 exact head

lessons: Writable CLI authority should remain narrowly delegated to the kernel boundary.
Cancellation preserves history and does not interrupt already-claimed work.
The command adds no clock, identity generation, dispatch, retry, permission, or execution authority.
